nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on keys and every 2-3 tree $t$ of height $h$, every key stored at a node of $t$ satisfies $p$ if and only if every element of the inorder flattening of $t$ satisfies $p$.
nodes.title: All-keys predicate agrees with the flattening on 2-3 trees

nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on keys and every 2-3 tree $t$ of height $h$, the recursive predicate requiring $p$ at every key stored at a node of $t$ holds if and only if $p(x)$ holds for every member $x$ of $t$, where $x$ is a member of $t$ when it equals one of the keys stored at some node of $t$.
nodes.title: All-keys predicate agrees with membership on 2-3 trees

nodes.summary: For a predicate $p$ on keys and a 2-3 tree $t$, $\mathrm{All}_p(t)$ states that every separator key stored at a node of $t$ satisfies $p$: it is true at a leaf, and at a node it requires $p$ of each key of the node and $\mathrm{All}_p$ of each of its subtrees.
nodes.title: Predicate on all keys of a 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: For every height $h$, every 2-3 tree of height $h$ satisfies the balance invariant: at every node, the subtrees are balanced and have equal computed heights.
nodes.title: Every height-indexed 2-3 tree is balanced

nodes.summary: For every root, that is, a 2-3 tree packaged with its height, the underlying height-indexed tree satisfies the balance invariant.
nodes.title: Every rooted 2-3 tree is balanced

nodes.summary: A leaf is balanced, and a node is balanced when all of its subtrees are balanced and have the same computed height, where the computed height of a tree is the length of its leftmost path from the root down to a leaf. Hence all leaves of a balanced tree lie at the same depth.
nodes.title: Balance invariant for 2-3 trees

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered key type, searching a root (a 2-3 tree packaged with its height) for a key $x$ returns the Boolean result of the 2-3 tree search for $x$ in the underlying height-indexed tree.
nodes.title: Search in a rooted 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered and let $t$ be a root (a 2-3 tree packaged with its height) whose underlying tree satisfies the ordering invariant. Then searching $t$ for a key $x$ returns true if and only if $x$ occurs in the inorder flattening of $t$.
nodes.title: Search in a rooted 2-3 tree is correct

nodes.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered and let $t$ be a 2-3 tree of height $h$ that satisfies the ordering invariant. Then searching $t$ for a key $x$ returns true if and only if $x$ occurs in the inorder flattening of $t$.
nodes.title: Search in an ordered 2-3 tree is correct

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered key type, searching a 2-3 tree for a key $x$ returns false at a leaf. At a 2-node with key $a$, it searches the left subtree if $x < a$, otherwise the right subtree if $a < x$, and otherwise returns true. At a 3-node with keys $a$ and $b$, it searches the left subtree if $x < a$; otherwise, if $a < x$, it searches the middle subtree if $x < b$, otherwise the right subtree if $b < x$, and…
nodes.title: Search in a 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: The empty 2-3 tree is the root of height $0$ whose underlying tree is the leaf.
nodes.title: Empty 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: The flattening of a 2-3 tree root is the flattening of its underlying tree, that is, the list of its keys in inorder.
nodes.title: Inorder traversal of a 2-3 tree root

nodes.summary: For every 2-3 tree $t$ (of any height) and every list $s$, the accumulated inorder traversal of $t$ onto $s$ equals the flattening of $t$ followed by $s$.
nodes.title: The accumulated traversal appends the suffix

nodes.summary: For a 2-3 tree $t$ and a list $s$, the accumulated traversal $F(t, s)$ is defined by recursion on $t$: for a leaf, $F(t, s) = s$; for a 2-node with key $a$ and children $l, r$, $F(t, s)$ is $F(l, s')$ where $s'$ is $a$ prepended to $F(r, s)$; for a 3-node with keys $a, b$ and children $l, m, r$, $F(t, s)$ is $F(l, s')$ where $s'$ is $a$ prepended to $F(m, s'')$ and $s''$ is $b$ prepended to $F(r, s)$.
nodes.title: Accumulated inorder traversal of a 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered, let $t$ be an ordered 2-3 tree root and let $x$ be a key. Then the flattening of the root obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ equals the ordered insertion of $x$ into the flattening of $t$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a 2-3 tree is ordered insertion into its traversal

nodes.summary: If the keys are linearly ordered and a 2-3 tree $t$ (of any height) is ordered, then no key occurs twice in the flattening of $t$.
nodes.title: The traversal of an ordered 2-3 tree has no duplicates

nodes.summary: The flattening of a 2-3 tree $t$ is the accumulated inorder traversal of $t$ onto the empty list. Equivalently, the flattening of a leaf is empty; that of a 2-node with key $a$ and children $l, r$ is the flattening of $l$, then $a$, then the flattening of $r$; and that of a 3-node with keys $a, b$ and children $l, m, r$ is the flattening of $l$, then $a$, then the flattening of $m$, then $b$, then the flattening of…
nodes.title: Inorder traversal of a 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: For linearly ordered keys, the 2-3 tree root built from a list is defined by recursion: the empty list gives the empty 2-3 tree, and a list with head $x$ and tail $xs$ gives the result of inserting $x$ into the root built from $xs$. Thus the elements are inserted into the empty tree from the last to the first.
nodes.title: Building a 2-3 tree from a list

nodes.summary: For every 2-3 tree $t$ with height index $h$, the height of $t$ computed along its leftmost spine equals $h$.
nodes.title: Computed height equals the height index

nodes.summary: For linearly ordered keys, every key $x$ and every 2-3 tree root $t$, the stored height of the root obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ is at most the stored height of $t$ plus one.
nodes.title: Insertion raises the height of a 2-3 tree by at most one

nodes.summary: For every root $t$, that is, a 2-3 tree together with its height index, the height of the underlying tree computed along its leftmost spine equals the stored height of $t$.
nodes.title: The stored height of a 2-3 tree root is its computed height

nodes.summary: The height of a 2-3 tree is computed along its leftmost spine: a leaf has height $0$, and a 2-node or a 3-node has height one more than the height of its leftmost child.
nodes.title: Height of a 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered, let $x \in \alpha$, and let $t$ be an ordered 2-3 tree of height $h$. Then inserting $x$ into $t$ meets the insertion specification. If the insertion returns a single tree $t'$ of height $h$, then $t'$ is ordered and its inorder traversal is the ordered insertion of $x$ into the inorder traversal of $t$. If it returns a split into trees $l$ and $r$ of height $h$ around a promoted…
nodes.title: Correctness of 2-3 tree insertion

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered, let $x \in \alpha$, and let $t$ be a 2-3 tree of height $h$. An insertion result of height $h$ meets the specification for inserting $x$ into $t$ when the following holds. If it is a single tree $t'$ of height $h$, then $t'$ is ordered and its inorder traversal equals the ordered insertion of $x$ into the inorder traversal of $t$. If it is a split into trees $l$ and $r$ of height…
nodes.title: Insertion specification for 2-3 trees

nodes.summary: Inserting a key $x$ into a 2-3 tree of height $h$ yields either a single tree of height $h$ or a split into two trees of height $h$ around a promoted key. Inserting into a leaf gives the split of two leaves around $x$. At a 2-node with key $a$, insertion recurses into the left child if $x < a$ and into the right child if $a < x$; a returned tree replaces that child, and a returned split around $k$ is absorbed by…
nodes.title: Insertion into a height-indexed 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: To insert a key $x$ into a root, that is, a 2-3 tree together with its height $h$, insert $x$ into the underlying tree. If this returns a single tree of height $h$, that tree is the new root, of height $h$. If it returns a split into trees $l$ and $r$ around a key $k$, the new root is the 2-node with key $k$ and children $l$ and $r$, of height $h + 1$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a 2-3 tree root

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered and let $t$ be an ordered 2-3 tree root over $\alpha$. For all $x, y \in \alpha$, $y$ occurs in the inorder traversal of the root obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ if and only if $y = x$ or $y$ occurs in the inorder traversal of $t$.
nodes.title: Keys after insertion into a 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: For every 2-3 tree $t$ of height $h$ and every key $x$, $x$ occurs in the inorder traversal of $t$ if and only if $x$ is a member of $t$, that is, one of the separator keys stored at its nodes.
nodes.title: The inorder traversal lists exactly the keys of a 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered. For every list $L$ over $\alpha$ and every $x \in \alpha$, $x$ occurs in the inorder traversal of the 2-3 tree built from $L$ (by inserting its elements from right to left into the empty tree) if and only if $x$ occurs in $L$.
nodes.title: Keys of a 2-3 tree built from a list

nodes.summary: A key $x$ is a member of a 2-3 tree when it is one of the separator keys stored at its nodes: nothing is a member of a leaf; $x$ is a member of a 2-node with key $a$ and children $l, r$ when it is a member of $l$, equals $a$, or is a member of $r$; and $x$ is a member of a 3-node with keys $a, b$ and children $l, m, r$ when it is a member of $l$, equals $a$, is a member of $m$, equals $b$, or is a member of $r$.
nodes.title: Membership in a 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $<$. A 2-3 tree of unspecified height over $\alpha$ is ordered when its underlying height-indexed 2-3 tree satisfies the ordering invariant.
nodes.title: Ordering invariant for 2-3 trees of unspecified height

nodes.summary: For every type $\alpha$ with a relation $<$, the empty 2-3 tree of unspecified height over $\alpha$ (the leaf, of height $0$) satisfies the ordering invariant.
nodes.title: The empty 2-3 tree is ordered

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every natural number $h$ and every ordered 2-3 tree $t$ over $\alpha$ of height $h$, the flattening (inorder traversal) of $t$ is strictly increasing: whenever a key $x$ occurs before a key $y$ in it, $x < y$.
nodes.title: Inorder traversal of an ordered 2-3 tree is strictly increasing

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every list $L$ of elements of $\alpha$, the 2-3 tree of unspecified height built from $L$, by inserting the elements of $L$ from right to left into the empty tree, is ordered.
nodes.title: Building a 2-3 tree from a list gives an ordered tree

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. If $t$ is an ordered 2-3 tree of unspecified height over $\alpha$ and $x \in \alpha$, then the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ is ordered.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves the ordering of 2-3 trees

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $<$. The leaf is ordered. A 2-node with separator $a$ and children $l$, $r$ is ordered when $l$ and $r$ are ordered, $y < a$ for every key $y$ stored in $l$, and $a < y$ for every key $y$ stored in $r$. A 3-node with separators $a$, $b$ and children $l$, $m$, $r$ is ordered when $l$, $m$ and $r$ are ordered, $a < b$, $y < a$ for every key $y$ stored in $l$, $a < y$ and $y < b$…
nodes.title: Ordering invariant for 2-3 trees

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ and a natural number $h$, an insertion result at height $h$ is either a 2-3 tree over $\alpha$ of height $h$, or a split: two 2-3 trees $l$ and $r$ over $\alpha$ of height $h$ together with a promoted key $k \in \alpha$.
nodes.title: Insertion results for 2-3 trees

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$, a 2-3 tree of unspecified height over $\alpha$ is a pair $(h, t)$ of a natural number $h$ and a height-indexed 2-3 tree $t$ over $\alpha$ of height $h$.
nodes.title: 2-3 trees of unspecified height

nodes.summary: An insertion result at height $h$ becomes a 2-3 tree of unspecified height as follows: a tree $t$ of height $h$ gives $t$ itself, of height $h$, and a split into trees $l$, $r$ of height $h$ around a key $k$ gives the 2-node with separator $k$, left child $l$ and right child $r$, of height $h + 1$.
nodes.title: Turning an insertion result into a 2-3 tree

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ of keys, the 2-3 trees over $\alpha$ indexed by height are generated as follows. The leaf is a tree of height $0$ and stores no key. For a natural number $h$, a key $a$ and trees $l$, $r$ of height $h$, the 2-node with separator $a$ and children $l$, $r$ is a tree of height $h + 1$. For a natural number $h$, keys $a$, $b$ and trees $l$, $m$, $r$ of height $h$, the 3-node with separators $a$, $b$…
nodes.title: Height-indexed 2-3 trees
Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
